elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: The retained warranty is only that "the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards" (9(b)(ii)) and that services "shall be free from errors that materially affect their utility" (9(b)(vi)). No "professional and workmanlike manner" performance standard was added, and the drafter expressly declined to seek it.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted 9(b)(xii): "the Auction Platform and any other software provided hereunder will conform in all material respects to the documentation provided by Kubient."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: The inserted conformance warranty runs "for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery", not twelve months.

9(b)(ii) and (vi) are unqualified ongoing warranties of the Service given in a covenanting clause ("represents, warrants and covenants"), with the compliance limb expressly running "throughout the Term"; an ongoing Term-length Service warranty exceeds a 90-day floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Kubient shall, at Customer's election, repair or replace the non-conforming software or Service".
Inserted: "or refund the fees paid for the non-conforming software or Service."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: 9(b)(ix): "it is now and throughout the Term shall comply with all applicable Laws in connection with the operation of its business and the performance of its obligations hereunder or the provision of the Service" (subject only to a materiality qualifier).

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: The rationale asserts 9(b) contains a no-malicious-code warranty, but no such limb appears in the cited or rendered text (only limbs (ii), (vi), (ix)-(xi) and the new (xii) are shown); the intervening subparagraphs were not supplied, so the element cannot be verified in operative language.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: New 9(b)(xii) gives an express software-to-documentation warranty for "a period of ninety (90) days following delivery" covering "the Auction Platform and any other software provided hereunder" — an express software warranty, not inferred from services conforming to a manual.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Retained 9(b)(ii) ("the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards") and (vi) (services "free from errors that materially affect their utility") are ongoing, unlimited-duration warranties within a Term-long warranty/covenant clause, comfortably exceeding 30 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted remedy sentence: "Kubient shall, at Customer's election, repair or replace the non-conforming software or Service", applying to breaches of the warranties in paragraph 9(b).
Inserted remedy sentence continues: "or refund the fees paid for the non-conforming software or Service."

reasons: All four fallback elements are met in operative language: the new 9(b)(xii) supplies the missing 90-day express software-to-documentation warranty, the new sentence supplies the previously absent repair/replace/refund remedy, and the retained ongoing Service warranties in 9(b)(ii) and (vi) exceed the 30-day services floor. The finding is correctly classified as a deviation cured at fallback.

Preferred is not reached: no "professional and workmanlike manner" services standard and only a 90-day (not 12-month) software conformance period; the no-malicious-code limb cannot be confirmed from the supplied text. These are noted as short of preferred, consistent with the drafter's own framing.

Minimality holds: the edit is a single concise insertion at the end of Kubient's existing warranty list, deletes nothing (including the Customer-favourable disclaimer carve-out "except for the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement"), and adds no survival tail, expense allocation, notice procedure or damages category outside the checklist. Electing "at Customer's election" rather than Vendor's option is a permissible Customer-side formulation of the same remedy element and adds no new requirement.

Intent is preserved: paragraph 13's express-warranty carve-out means the new warranty is not swallowed by the AS IS disclaimer; no cross-reference is broken and no retained sentence contradicts the insertion. "documentation provided by Kubient" is lower-case descriptive language, not an undefined capitalised term, so it creates no dangling definition.

Two watch-items for the drafter, neither fatal: (1) confirm "Auction Platform" is a defined term elsewhere in the Agreement, otherwise substitute "the Service" to avoid a dangling reference; (2) the remedy sentence is drafted to cover breach of all warranties "in this paragraph 9(b)" — this is broader than the two remedy elements strictly require, though it is Customer-favourable and does not import any new obligation, so it does not defeat minimality. If Vendor pushes back, narrowing it to the conformance and Service performance warranties is the cleanest retreat.
